title: Cranberry Orange Sauce
subtitle: fresh cranberries simmered with orange until they burst, then left to set: ten minutes, and miles better than the can
imageAlt: Glossy whole-berry cranberry sauce with orange zest in a white bowl with a spoon
servingsNote: about 2 cups: for Christmas dinner, sandwiches and morning toast

beforeYouStart.text: Use a medium saucepan; the berries foam up as they pop.
Frozen cranberries go straight in, no thawing. Add 1–2 minutes to the simmer.

steps.title: Dissolve the sugar
steps.text: Bring the sugar, orange juice and water to a boil in a medium saucepan over medium-high, stirring until the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the cranberries and salt. Simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring now and then, until most of the berries have burst and the sauce starts to thicken.

steps.title: Finish and cool
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the orange zest. Cool to room temperature, about 1 hour (it sets as it cools), then refrigerate.

fixIt.fix: Stir in sugar 1 tbsp at a time while it's still warm.
Give it time: it thickens a lot as it cools. If it's still loose once cold, simmer 3–4 minutes more.
Stir in a spoonful or two of water or orange juice.

saleTip: Fresh cranberries are about $3–4 a bag at No Frills in November and December. Buy an extra bag for the freezer; they keep a year.
swap: All water instead of orange juice gives the pure, tart classic. A cinnamon pinch or a spoon of maple syrup are both nice additions.
leftovers: Swirl into yogurt or oatmeal, spread in a leftover sandwich, or spoon over brie.
doneness: Done when most berries have popped and the sauce coats a spoon; it thickens a lot as it cools.
source: Based on the classic cranberry sauce ratio printed on the bag (340 g berries, sugar, 1 cup liquid), with orange juice for half the water and a little less sugar.
prepAhead: Make it up to a week before Christmas and keep it in the fridge. It's best made at least a day ahead.
reheat: Serve cold or at room temperature. To warm it, heat gently in a small pot 2–3 minutes with a splash of water.

basic.note: The straight classic: berries, sugar and water.

stepNotes.0: Basic: use water in place of the orange juice.
stepNotes.2: Basic: no zest; just cool and chill.

fancy.note: Maple and a pinch of cinnamon.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: stir in the maple syrup and cinnamon with the zest.

plating: Serve in a small glass bowl so the colour shows.
A few strands of zest on top.

why.0-0: Cranberries are full of natural pectin, so the sauce gels on its own as it cools.
why.0-5: A pinch of salt makes the fruit taste brighter, not salty.

funFact: Ripe cranberries bounce. Growers used to sort them by bouncing them down wooden steps; firm ones made it over the barrier and soft ones didn't.

keeps.note: freeze in a jar with room at the top
keeps.thaw: Overnight in the fridge, then stir; serve cold or warm it gently

pairs: a spoon on top of the stuffing
